searchText: I'm glad you asked this question. I don't follow EIPs cause my main interest is on ETH2, but I experienced the very same thing that you are mentioning. I started tracking closely my ETH2 client of choice and realized that actually the specs move faster than what the software engineers can follow at times. Luckily for us there's a centralized place where the interface between protocol and implementation takes place, and the specs repo is a canonical place to look at. I think you are out of luck on Eth1 though. In any case, my (very short) experience following the specs repo gives me the impression that very very few people are actually following the details of what's going on in depth (it's reasonable given the pace and breath) and that development happens much faster than what I would have liked it. but if you are literally asking for a centralized place to look at EIPs try https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs yes, you should follow <#746566142700814426> - and chat with Pooja and Micah here - they're really involved in the process if you check in with the core dev call every two weeks that's a pretty good cadence where roadmap and implementation decisions are discussed do you have examples that come to mind for "issues between the documented and actual" In the respective project's server. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Nz8YrCC9X8&t=77s yes, exactly. Thats my problem rn, but I think it could be meaningless when having more experience on that (im a newbie here) perfect, will follow then for instance, yesterday night I was trying to know whats the value of the latest bomb delay. The YP current version says 5M and googling didnt help to get the actual value, but just get 9.7M proposal is in draft. Finally I just reverse-engineered the actual value of recent blocks and saw its 9M as per eip-2384 oh the yellow paper wouldn't have that updated value yet, as London isn't live yet Watching Vitalik's interview with Lex Fridman today while working on my side projects. 👍 Please keep conversation in this server Research and Development focused, even in the <#595721451651465227> channel. its a good interview though, maybe should drop it in 'education channel' being able to communicate (and understand 🙂 ) these complicated topics really well is something I want to be able to do got it, thx! i think the YP is even farther behind than that... not sure when it was last updated tbh I think the torquem guys update it to Petersburg, not sure if it has the updated value though https://torquem.ch/yellow_paper_petersburg.pdf TIL that torquem is a group lol and I am pretty tapped in Haha me too, curiousity helps 🙂 The YP repository uses different branches for different versions: https://github.com/ethereum/yellowpaper/blob/master/BRANCHES.md What's the different between the ethereum magicians and the ethereum research discourse forum? I see EIPs been submitted for discussion on both forums 😅 ETHresearch is for more high level theoretical research and ideas, generally related to Ethereum, sometimes others ETHmagicians is more for figuring out how to get those ideas implemented, and the process by which that happens. (aka the EIP process) Nice, very succinct. Thanks <@!420951281910284289> I am trying to figure out the best ways to start contributing in Solidity related projects. Gitcoin is a bit chaotic, so I was reading through the forums to participate in the Ethereum Application layer, check out the Crypto Devs discord servers. tons of solidity devs there!
